instructions: Read the passage and choose one answer for each question.
passage:
Maya wants to send a birthday gift to her sister, Noor, who has moved to another city. Noor collects small cups made by local artists. Maya has found a blue cup at a weekend market, and she writes a short letter about the artist who made it. She puts the letter in an envelope but leaves the envelope open until she has checked the spelling of Noor's name. Maya also finds an old stamp in a drawer. It is pretty, but the clerk later explains that this stamp is for a letter, not for the box she wants to post.

Maya brings her mail to the neighborhood office and asks a clerk how to prepare the parcel. The recipient is Noor, so the address must be complete and easy to read. Maya copies the street name from her sister's message and adds the zip code. The clerk explains that the code helps the local service sort the item. Maya notices that the first number she wrote is wrong. She checks the message again before she closes anything.

The cup is fragile, so Maya uses soft paper to wrap it. Her priority is to keep the cup safe throughout the journey. She places it inside a box made of thick cardboard and fills the empty space with more paper. The clerk explains that a sturdy container helps protect the cup. When she gently moves the box, the cup does not move. She uses tape to seal the top and writes the address on the side. The clerk asks her to confirm the address one last time. The clerk also asks whether the recipient will be at home for a delivery that needs a signature. Noor has already told Maya that she can be home on Thursday afternoon.

Maya asks about the difference between a domestic shipment and an overseas one. At this fictional office, a domestic item goes to a place in the same country, while an overseas item goes abroad. An overseas parcel may need a declaration that describes what is inside. Because Noor lives in the same country, Maya does not need that form for this parcel. The clerk gives her the fee for the domestic option before Maya pays. The distance is not the only thing that affects the fee; the size of the box matters too.

After Maya pays, the clerk will dispatch the parcel the next morning. Maya receives a small slip as proof that she paid. She asks about insurance, but decides not to add it after she hears the terms. The slip is an official record from this imaginary office, not a promise that every postal service has the same rules. Maya sends Noor a message with the expected day. Noor replies that she is excited to receive the gift, and Maya is relieved that she checked the code before leaving.
